newsitem.title: USA: FDIC rescinds duplicative bank derivative rule.
newsitem.headline: FDIC rescinds duplicative bank derivative rule.

text.p: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp said its board of directors voted to rescind a 17-year-old policy statement on derivatives that had been superseded by more recent regulations.
The board rescinded the 1979 Policy Statement regarding the use of interest rate futures contracts, forward contracts and standby contracts.

Since that statement was issued, the FDIC said it has issued more comprehensive guidance on both oversight of derivatives and interest rate risk management, "making the 1979 policy statement outmoded and duplicative."

FDIC said its more recent rules on derivatives are the May 18, 1994 Financial Institution Letter 34-94, Examination Guidance on Financial Derivatives, the Joint Policy Statement: Interest Rate Risk, issued with other bank regulatory agencies June 26, 1996, and instructions for the Consolidated Reports of Condition and Income.
